$comment: P7-06: fictional visitors for the live interview check (pnpm eval:interviews). Six scripted answers each, one per stage of a six-question interview. Invented people; nothing here is anyone's real words.

setup.name: Priya
setup.about: I run three neighbourhood bakeries in Bristol.

answers: I run three bakeries in Bristol. We start at four every morning and most of what we sell is sourdough and cardamom buns.
It started in my mum's kitchen in Leicester. She baked for the whole street at Diwali and I was the one carrying trays door to door.
The second shop nearly sank us. The landlord tripled the rent after a year and I had to choose between closing it or taking a loan against my flat.
I took the loan. For eighteen months I didn't pay myself and I missed my brother's wedding because we were short-staffed that weekend.
Cost your time honestly. I used to think my hours were free, and they were the most expensive thing in the business.
Now it's the team. Two of my bakers started as weekend staff at sixteen and one of them is about to run the third shop.

setup.name: Tom
setup.about: Software engineer, now building a scheduling app for clinics.

answers: I build software that helps small physio clinics fill cancelled appointments. Before that I was a backend engineer at a bank for nine years.
My wife is a physio. She'd come home furious about no-shows, and one night I wrote a script that texted her waiting list when a slot opened.
The turning point was when a clinic in Manchester asked to pay for the script. I quit the bank three months later, which terrified me.
Honestly, the fear was about being wrong in public. My dad thought leaving the bank was reckless and he still asks when I'll get a proper job.
Talk to ten customers before you write a line of code. I got lucky that my first customer lived in my house.
What matters now is that the product stays boring and reliable. Clinics don't want features, they want a full diary.

setup.about: Former ICU nurse, now a product manager in health tech.

answers: I spent eleven years as an ICU nurse and now I'm a product manager for software that monitors patients after surgery.
During the pandemic I was charting on paper at three in the morning while a monitor beeped at me, and I kept thinking someone should fix this.
A doctor I trusted introduced me to a start-up that needed a clinician. I said yes before I understood what a product manager did.
I felt like a fraud for the first year. Engineers would talk in acronyms and I'd nod along, then look everything up on the bus home.
Your frontline experience is the asset, not a gap. Stop apologising for not knowing the jargon and say what you've seen on the ward.
I want nurses to finish a shift with ten fewer minutes of paperwork. That's the whole goal, and it's harder than it sounds.

setup.name: Jonas
setup.about: Ich bin Tischler und habe eine kleine Werkstatt in Leipzig.

answers: Ich baue Möbel auf Maß in meiner Werkstatt in Leipzig, vor allem Küchen und Regale für Altbauwohnungen mit schiefen Wänden.
Angefangen hat es bei meinem Großvater in der Garage. Er hat mir mit zwölf einen Hobel geschenkt und gesagt, ich solle ihn nie verleihen.
Der Wendepunkt war ein Auftrag für ein Café, das plötzlich in einer Zeitschrift stand. Danach kamen drei Monate lang jeden Tag Anfragen.
Es hat mich meine Gesundheit gekostet. Ich habe zwei Jahre lang sechs Tage die Woche gearbeitet und irgendwann hatte ich Rückenprobleme.
Nimm nicht jeden Auftrag an. Die schlechtesten Kunden waren immer die, bei denen ich schon beim ersten Gespräch ein ungutes Gefühl hatte.
Heute ist mir wichtig, dass ich abends um sechs die Werkstatt zumache und meine Tochter vom Kindergarten abhole.
I'm an accountant.
Fell into it after uni.
Got made partner last year.
Long hours.
Get good at Excel.
My kids.
